declarations.docstring: Morphisms between representations after reflection at a distinguished vertex.
The component maps commute with arrows away from the distinguished vertex.
The sum of the reflected component contributions vanishes at the distinguished vertex.
Reflection morphisms are determined by their component maps away from the distinguished vertex.
Returns the linear component of a reflection morphism at a non-distinguished vertex.
States that the two displayed reflected morphism spaces admit an equivalence.
Arrow maps agree heterogeneously after transporting the quiver structure.
Provides a vertexwise linear equivalence after reindexing a representation along equal quivers.
The reindexing equivalences intertwine the transported arrow maps.
The object assigned to each vertex is unchanged by quiver reindexing.
Gives the vertexwise equivalence between a reflected representation and its original indexing.
The reflection reindexing equivalences commute with the corresponding arrow maps.
The reflected arrow maps coincide heterogeneously after the indexing transport.
The reflected and original vertex objects are equal after reindexing.
The vertex recorded by an outgoing-arrow index differs from the distinguished vertex.
The vertex recorded by an incoming-arrow index differs from the distinguished vertex.
States that the displayed reflected morphism space is equivalent to the reflection-morphism type.
Constructs the equivalence between the displayed reflected morphism space and reflection morphisms.
States the dual orientation of the reflected morphism-space equivalence.
Constructs the dual orientation of the reflected morphism-space equivalence.
Describes the reflected arrow map on a single direct-sum summand.
Extracts the arrow into the distinguished vertex represented by an index.
Identifies the extracted arrow with the arrow stored in its index.
Extracting the arrow from a constructed index returns the original arrow.
Reconstructing an index from its extracted arrow returns its stored arrow data.
Transporting an arrow through the index conversion and back leaves it unchanged.
Applying the map from the direct sum equals the sum of its arrow-map components.
Applying the map from the direct sum to one summand is its associated arrow map.
Equates the two index types associated with the distinguished vertex.
